draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Cherai Beach! It's a long, golden beach on Vypin island, with the sea on one side and backwaters on the other. Sometimes dolphins swim close to the shore.
draft.hungryLine: Cherai eats fish, prawns and crab, fresh from both the sea and the backwaters.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the beach, then cross to the backwater side to see the Chinese fishing nets.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a chair on the sand and stay for the sunset over the sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Pallipuram Fort, just up the road, was built by the Portuguese in 1503. It's one of the oldest European buildings in India.

legends.title: A fort with six sides
legends.body: Pallipuram Fort is a small six-sided tower. The Portuguese built it to guard the way into Kochi.

legends.title: Dolphins by the shore
legends.body: On calm mornings, dolphins are sometimes spotted just beyond the waves.

tips.title: Fresh crab is priced by weight.

story.title: An island is born
story.body: The great Periyar flood that opened Kochi's harbour also shaped Vypin island.

story.title: The Portuguese fort
story.body: The Portuguese built Pallipuram Fort, one of the oldest European buildings still standing in India.

story.title: Fishing villages
story.body: Families fished the sea on one side and the backwaters on the other.

story.title: A favourite beach
story.body: Cherai became the go-to beach for Kochi families.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Beach, fort, then the fishing nets at sunset. Tell me if you saw a dolphin.

food.name: Seafood shacks at Cherai
